comments.body: I have a question. If you use Fine tribute goods on a player pirate can they farm you again or are you protected by the 24 hour rule?

comments.author: Erda
comments.body:
When using fine tributes it will give half your current money directly on you to the pirate and the battle ends

AND

You get a green flag effect which last 5mins. During this 5 minutes you cannot be attacked by any other players enough time to get the hell out of dodge. Also every time you tribute a player it will count as a kill for the pirate player which will count towards their 5/5 kill limit.

comments.author: Hans
comments.body: The 24 hour rule only applies if the pirate actually sinks you weather it's through melee, cannons, or losing at DB. If you use a tribute and the pirate is following you afterwards you should log out, or try to out-sail and lose him/her somehow. As Erda pointed out, it still technically counts as a kill regardless if they sink you or not. And after 5 kills, pirates must head to either Jolo or Nassau to reset it.

comments.author: Lena
comments.body: Actually if you use a tribute the 24 hour rule *does* apply. My friend confirmed it through experiment. I also suspect it applies when you successfully run away from the battle too, but I have no definite proof.

comments.author: H.-Gazi
comments.body:
Summary:
Fine tribute goods is used to end the battle against player pirates/privateer. Each player within the fleet will lose half of their ducats (from pocket) in exchange for a secure release. After that your whole fleet is 5 minutes protected from any PVP attacks (green flag).

Can be used:
By white players who are attacked in hostile waters by player pirates/privateers

Can't be used:
> Against NPC pirates
> In Lawless waters
> By player pirates/privateer

Furthermore, for the NO.3 recipe I did Luxor dungeon to get those Jewellery and Antique Arts to make these chests.

Hope this makes clear for the most of them. :-)

comments.author: BIakeC
comments.body: Mid FSD floor also drops half the stuff needed to make fine tribute goods (Sapphire, Gold, and Jewellery). If you have room, save them in your quarters or shared storage rather then selling them off willy nilly.
